Cliff Sosin on why demand for frontier AI may narrow as models get smarter:

"It's like this diamond-shaped demand frontier, where initially, you get wider and wider uses, and then it starts to get more and more rarefied. How often do you really need a 300 IQ?

It strikes me as totally reasonable that there are very few use cases for super elite intelligence. 

There are lots of use cases for very good intelligence. That very good intelligence is highly competitive and commoditized.

How big is the market if good enough intelligence is very, very cheap?"

THE DAILY METALS PULSE — WEEKEND EDITION ☕
Equities battered. Gold below $3,900. Silver around $49.
A painful finish to October. Yet there are positive signals worth watching beneath the selling.

☢️ URANIUM IS MOVING HIGHER

The indicative uranium price reached US$92.55/lb on Friday, up roughly 3.5% over the past month.

Cameco’s latest published long-term indicator stood at $96.50/lb at September-end, compared with $86.50 at the end of 2025.

And Friday’s quarterly report highlighted utilities seeking uranium supply, with several requests for proposals requiring responses before year-end.

That matters. Fuel procurement is moving forward while equity investors are retreating. Existing reactors, life extensions and new construction underpin demand well beyond the latest AI earnings scare.

🟡 GOLD: CENTRAL BANKS ARE STILL BUYING

The World Gold Council reported 39 tonnes of net central-bank purchases in August. Official-sector accumulation remains a supportive factor, even while liquidation and interest-rate expectations dominate short-term prices.

⚪ SILVER: THE DEFICIT STORY REMAINS

The Silver Institute’s 2026 survey forecasts a sixth consecutive annual supply deficit—even with weaker industrial demand. Falling prices alone cannot replenish inventories drawn down over several years.

🟠 COPPER: PHYSICAL DEMAND SHOWS RESILIENCE

China’s Yangshan import premium remained near a 13-year high on Friday. Buyers paying more to secure physical metal is an encouraging signal amid the wider market weakness.

📅 THE TAX-LOSS WINDOW

November and December can bring additional selling pressure to losing positions, particularly less-liquid resource shares.

For patient investors with room to add, that can create opportunities to build positions gradually before seasonal selling subsides. Cash, dilution risk and credible project milestones still matter. A rebound is never automatic.

Two of my sponsors offer specific reasons to keep watching:

🇺🇸 MYRIAD URANIUM — $M.CN $MYRUF
Its 100%-owned Copper Mountain project in Wyoming combines extensive historical exploration with fresh Phase II uranium intersections. Progress towards a modern resource estimate offers a tangible catalyst; the latest radiometric results remain subject to laboratory verification.

🇨🇦 SKYHARBOUR — $SYH $SYHBF
At Getty East in the Russell Lake project area, Denison is funding approximately 3,600 metres of drilling. That gives Skyharbour exposure to Athabasca discovery potential while sharing the financial burden through its partner’s earn-in.

The combination worth watching: improving uranium prices, active exploration and weaker share prices.
That is where a difficult market can start creating opportunity.

$HG $HGRAF #Graphene

A tyre manufacturer wants longer life. A shipowner wants less corrosion. A data-centre operator needs to remove more heat.

HydroGraph’s graphene could help all three.

Its application work targets expensive problems across industries:

🛞 TYRES — Reinforce rubber to improve wear resistance and durability. Longer-lasting tyres could lower replacement costs and waste.

🛡️ COATINGS — Slow the penetration of water and oxygen, helping protect ships, bridges and industrial equipment from corrosion.

🏗️ CONCRETE — Reduce cement consumption while preserving strength. HG reports equivalent 28-day compressive strength with 20% less cement in tests.

🚗 PLASTICS — Reduce component weight and material use. HG reports 30% lightweighting in customer programmes.

⚙️ LUBRICANTS — Reduce friction and protect moving parts. HG reports 70% less wear in engine-oil testing.

❄️ AI COOLING — Improve heat transfer through graphene-enhanced cooling fluids and thermal interface materials.

The attraction is the economics. Less material. Less maintenance. Longer service life. Better performance from products manufacturers already sell.

Now imagine just ONE major tyre manufacturer qualifying HydroGraph’s graphene for widespread use.

An illustrative 1 gram per tyre across 100 million tyres would require 100 tonnes of graphene every year. Actual dosage and adoption would depend on qualification. The market is huge: worldwide, around 2.6 billion tyres were produced in 2025.

A tiny ingredient can become substantial recurring demand when it goes into millions of products.

HydroGraph’s October update says multiple advanced customers have progressed into negotiations covering prices, volumes and supply terms. The first larger purchase orders are expected within 2026.

The issue is that the content has nothing that is relevant for people like myself and there is a large population of people like me.

That’s why you’ll very likely not see me at a crypto fintech conference, but you will at Devcon regardless whatever country it ends up in.

BREAKING NEWS🚨: HBM CHIPS CAN REACH OVER 1000 tok/s/user on giant 700B+ models via agent swarm-written software, according to a new NVIDIA AgentX submission.

Furthermore, on Rubin NVL72, it can achieve 20.9x better perf per TCO than GB300 NVL72 at even "ultrafast" speeds of 325 tok/s/user and up to 9.11x better perf per TCO at 200 tok/s/user. (1/2)🧵
